correctness.rationale: Complete modular valuation proof: for d=2^k u with u odd≥3 a length-d comparison interval necessarily includes a mismatch (q≡2 or3 mod4), so repetition periods are dyadic; all dyadic repetitions start at a≥2d and have length≤4d−1, hence endpoint <3a. The explicit dyadic blocks are squares by valuation parity at the unique exceptional boundary. These imply the all-r lower and upper bounds without finite inference. Independent exact checker verified 5518 bounded square occurrences, all 13 proposed dyadic squares, and DP shortest widths for r=1,…,10; finite limits are documented.

originality.rationale: The inspected primary repetition-factorization paper (arXiv:2311.14961) provides the invariant and proves bounded shortest widths for other automatic words, but has no period-doubling shortest-width theorem. The same-object least-period study (arXiv:1207.5450) concerns a weaker property (periods of factors with no exponent restriction). Same-object pattern-avoidance and kernel/gap-factorization papers do not imply the explicit unbounded minimum-width family. Exact statement, aliases, and stronger-covering results were searched; unindexed or implicit prior work is a residual risk.
residual_risks: An equivalent period-doubling shortest-width result may exist in unindexed literature or as an unextracted consequence of a complete square-structure classification.

value.rationale: The minimum number of repetition factors is directly motivated by the source paper and its unbounded-shortest-width question. The result provides a new classical automatic-word instance with log-scale lower/upper bounds along explicit factors, plus a global structural lemma on all repetition factors. Bounded monochromatic runs ensure the effect is not merely a trivial result of long constant runs. An exact value for every witness or an arbitrary-word decidability theorem is neither necessary nor claimed.
